name: Senso-ji Temple
description: Tokyo's oldest temple, known for its bright lantern gate and lively shopping street.
detailedDescription: Senso-ji Temple is one of Tokyo's most visited cultural landmarks. Visitors enter through Kaminarimon Gate, walk along Nakamise-dori for snacks and souvenirs, and arrive at the main hall where traditional architecture sits in the middle of modern Asakusa.
hours: Temple grounds open daily; main hall usually 6:00 AM - 5:00 PM
access: Short walk from Asakusa Station on the Ginza, Asakusa, or Tobu Skytree lines.

name: Shibuya Crossing
description: A famous scramble crossing surrounded by neon signs, shops, and city energy.
detailedDescription: Shibuya Crossing is a classic Tokyo experience where crowds move across the intersection from every direction. The area is surrounded by department stores, cafes, music venues, and viewpoints that make it a great first stop for seeing the city's pace.
access: Outside Shibuya Station, near the Hachiko Exit.

name: Ueno Park
description: A spacious park with museums, temples, a zoo, and cherry blossoms in spring.
detailedDescription: Ueno Park combines nature, history, and museums in one easy-to-visit area. It is especially popular during cherry blossom season, but the Tokyo National Museum, Shinobazu Pond, and walking paths make it useful for almost any Tokyo itinerary.
hours: Park open daily; museums and attractions vary
price: Park is free; museums and zoo have separate fees
access: A few minutes on foot from Ueno Station.

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
description: A shrine famous for thousands of red torii gates winding up Mount Inari.
detailedDescription: Fushimi Inari Taisha is dedicated to Inari, the deity of rice and prosperity. The shrine's paths pass through long tunnels of red torii gates, leading visitors from the main shrine area into quiet wooded trails on the mountain.
access: Directly outside Inari Station on the JR Nara Line.

name: Kinkaku-ji
description: The Golden Pavilion, a shining Zen temple reflected in a peaceful pond.
detailedDescription: Kinkaku-ji is one of Kyoto's most recognizable sights. Its upper floors are covered in gold leaf, and the temple is viewed from a garden path that frames the building, pond, islands, and surrounding trees.
access: Reachable by Kyoto City Bus from Kyoto Station or Kitaoji Station.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
description: A scenic bamboo path near temples, river views, and mountain scenery.
detailedDescription: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is a short but memorable walking path through tall bamboo stalks that sway overhead. The surrounding district includes Tenryu-ji Temple, Togetsukyo Bridge, small shops, and peaceful river views.
access: Walk from Saga-Arashiyama Station or Arashiyama Station.

name: Dotonbori
description: A bright canal district known for street food, signs, and nightlife.
detailedDescription: Dotonbori is one of Osaka's best places to experience food culture. Visitors can try takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and ramen while walking past giant restaurant signs, the canal, and the famous Glico running man sign.
access: Walk from Namba Station or Osaka-Namba Station.

name: Osaka Castle
description: A historic castle museum surrounded by stone walls, moats, and parkland.
detailedDescription: Osaka Castle is a major symbol of the city. The reconstructed main tower contains a museum about Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Osaka's history, while the surrounding park is popular for walking and seasonal flowers.
price: About 600 yen for the castle tower
access: Walk from Osakajokoen, Morinomiya, or Tanimachi 4-chome Station.

name: Shinsekai
description: A retro neighborhood centered around Tsutenkaku Tower and local food.
detailedDescription: Shinsekai has an old Osaka atmosphere with colorful signs, casual restaurants, and the landmark Tsutenkaku Tower. It is especially known for kushikatsu, a local fried skewer dish served in lively restaurants.
access: Walk from Dobutsuen-mae Station or Shin-Imamiya Station.

name: Ohori Park
description: A relaxing city park with a large pond, walking paths, and boat rentals.
detailedDescription: Ohori Park is a calm green space near central Fukuoka. Its pond and loop path make it good for walking, jogging, or resting between city stops, and the nearby Japanese garden adds a more traditional setting.
price: Free; some nearby facilities charge admission
access: Short walk from Ohori Koen Station.

name: Canal City Hakata
description: A large shopping and entertainment complex built around a canal.
detailedDescription: Canal City Hakata combines shops, restaurants, theaters, hotels, and fountain shows in one complex. It is an easy indoor stop for meals and shopping, especially on rainy days or between train connections.
hours: Shops usually 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM; restaurants vary
access: Walk from Hakata Station or Kushida Shrine Station.

name: Dazaifu Tenmangu
description: A famous shrine dedicated to learning, surrounded by historic streets.
detailedDescription: Dazaifu Tenmangu is dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, a scholar associated with education. Students often visit to pray for exam success, and the approach to the shrine has cafes, souvenir shops, and local sweets.
hours: Usually 6:30 AM - 7:00 PM; varies by season
access: Walk from Dazaifu Station on the Nishitetsu line.

name: Odori Park
description: A long central park in Sapporo known for festivals and seasonal displays.
detailedDescription: Odori Park stretches through the center of Sapporo and hosts major events like the Snow Festival, autumn food festival, and summer beer garden. It is a useful starting point for exploring the city on foot.
access: Next to Odori Station in central Sapporo.

name: Otaru Canal
description: A preserved canal area lined with old warehouses, lamps, and shops.
detailedDescription: Otaru Canal offers a slower coastal-city atmosphere near Sapporo. Historic stone warehouses now hold cafes, museums, and shops, while the canal path is especially pretty in the evening when lamps reflect on the water.

name: Shirogane Blue Pond
description: A striking blue pond near Biei with pale tree trunks rising from the water.
detailedDescription: Shirogane Blue Pond is known for its unusual blue color, which changes with the weather and season. The pond is a popular photography stop near Biei and pairs well with nearby scenic drives through central Hokkaido.
hours: Open daily; viewing times may vary in winter
access: Best reached by car or bus from Biei Station.
